## Leaking Ceiling Checklist for a London Tenant

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg

You already did the most important first step: you notified the landlord by email on the same day. Since the leak is limited to one bedroom and there’s no electrical damage, the priority now is clear evidence, tidy records, and a firm follow-up asking for action.

## Evidence, Repair Records, and Follow-Up Message

### 1) What to collect right away
- Photos of the leak from multiple angles, including the ceiling, any staining, bubbling paint, drips, and nearby furniture/flooring
- A short video showing the active leak and how fast it is dripping, if it is still happening
- Time-stamped notes: date discovered, when you emailed the landlord, and any replies
- A simple room map or note identifying exactly where the leak is in the bedroom
- Photos of any temporary protection you used, such as buckets, towels, or plastic sheeting
- Copies of the tenancy agreement, inventory, and your original email to the landlord

### 2) How to document repairs and impact
- Keep one running log with date, time, who you spoke to, and what was said
- Save every email in a single folder and, if possible, export them as PDFs
- Photograph the ceiling again after any visit or repair so you can compare before/after
- Note any contractor details: company name, visit date, what they inspected, and what they did
- Record practical impact only: unusable bed space, moved furniture, sleep disruption, smell, stains, or repeated dampness
- If the leak changes or spreads, take new photos immediately and add a fresh note

### 3) What to ask for in the follow-up
- Acknowledgment that the report was received
- An inspection or repair visit date
- A written update on the cause of the leak
- A timeline for next steps
- Confirmation of who will attend and when you should expect contact
- A request to keep you informed if access to the flat is needed

### 4) Clear follow-up message you can send
Subject: Follow-up on ceiling leak in bedroom — reported 18 April 2025

Hello [Landlord/Agent Name],

I’m following up on the ceiling leak in the bedroom that I reported by email on 18 April 2025. The leak is still affecting the room, although there has been no electrical damage.

Could you please confirm:
- when this will be inspected or repaired
- who will be attending
- the likely timeframe for the next update

I have kept photos and notes of the issue in case they are helpful. Please let me know if you need access to the flat or any further details from me.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Flat address]
[Phone number]

### 5) Practical checklist for the next 24 hours
- Take dated photos and one short video
- Save the original email and any reply
- Start a simple incident log
- Protect the area and move belongings away from the leak
- Send the follow-up message if you have not received a prompt response
- Keep monitoring for any change in size, smell, staining, or dampness

## Tenant Action Plan for the Leak

| Step | Action | What to keep | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Photograph the leak | Wide shot, close-up, room context | Clear visual record |
| 2 | Save the original report | Sent email, timestamp, recipient | Proof of prompt notice |
| 3 | Log every contact | Date, time, name, outcome | Repair timeline trail |
| 4 | Track repairs | Visit date, contractor name, notes | Record of action taken |
| 5 | Follow up in writing | Short email requesting update | Clear request for next step |

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Email follow-up] <mailto:>
